title: Summary
text: PlanetScope imagery provides global, high-resolution (~3-meter), near-daily data, making valuable scientific research monitoring phenology [@moon2021phenology], land use change, disaster impacts, . Planet API facilitates access [@planet2017api], using data remains challenging due complex API interactions, limits large-volume data downloads, non-trivial processing workflows, can hinder reproducibility. Existing options include official Planet Python SDK, cloud-based platforms like Sentinel Hub Google Earth Engine (GEE), R package planetR [@bevington2024planetr]. However, Python JavaScript used first three platforms may less familiar R users. Cloud platforms also restrict user control processing environments local data storage. Furthermore, existing tools typically require users write extensive custom scripts batch downloading processing across multiple sites, process often limited computing storage resources. BatchPlanet addresses gaps providing R-native tool batch access processing PlanetScope imagery (Table 1). streamlined, parallelized functions designed scalability, transparency, reproducibility scientific data pipelines. package supported peer-reviewed research predicting reproductive phenology wind-pollinated trees [@song2025phenology].
